text.p: Constellation Energy Corp, a new company to be born out of a pending utilities merger, filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $300 million in medium-term notes.

Constellation Energy will be the name for the yet to be approved merger between Baltimore Gas and Electric Co and Potomac Electric Power Co which would form one of the largest utilities in the country, worth $15 billion.

The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission plans to rule April 16 on the proposed merger. The utilities are also still waiting from the District of Columbia Public Service Commission and the Maryland Public Service Commission.
The notes, series F, are in minimum denominations of $1,000, increased in multiples of $1,000 and interest is paid on fixed rate notes on May 1 and November 1, among others, the April 9 filing said.

Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes relating to the utility business, including repayment of commercial paper borrowings used to finance construction, other capital expenditures and operations.
The new company will be based in Annapolis, Maryland.
Constellation Energy has not yet filed for a stock symbol.
The proposed sale of the notes has not been approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission nor any state securities commission, the filing said.
